authorshipNote: Authored by Eugene (per plan Decision (d), B1 is the incident anchor and owns Eugene's judgement). Drafted with Cowork assistance 2026-04-20.
notes: Each entry below uses mustMatch='substring' where variants are expected (e.g. surname appears as 'Ms Ferguson', 'Ferguson', 'Melissa Ferguson'), and 'exact' where the detection should match the precise string.

Some type assignments are deliberately conservative — e.g. medical diagnosis prose is typed 'personal-name' under s7(2)(a) rather than 'health-safety' (which is about public protective measures, not individual diagnoses). The v3.2 plan amendment discussed adding a new worked example for this pattern.

Witness names in the Interviews table and Findings section are typed 'harassment-risk' (s7(2)(f)(ii)) because the document is a bullying grievance — witness identities must be protected per Phase 3 Example 11 pattern.
Organisation names (Awatere Medical Centre, Holroyd Partners) are typed 'confidential' with ground s7(2)(a) — type 'personal-name' is specifically for individuals.
Salary-band rows are typed 'confidential' with ground s7(2)(a) — individual compensation is privacy-sensitive PII but doesn't fit any other dedicated type.

expectedDetections.rationale: Investigator's name — appears in the header table and the Prepared-by signoff on page 4. Third-party council staff in grievance context; plan's Phase 3 reworded carve-out should include her.
External counsel (Holroyd Partners) named in the header and in the commentary section. Third-party professional — flaggable under v3.1 Phase 3 Example 15 pattern.
External legal firm named alongside privileged advice — protect to preserve privilege context. Debatable: could also be released as the firm's identity is already disclosed in other council records.

Surname appears many times across pages 2-3 in prose. Phase 4 entity propagation test case — only B1 test case after Phase 4 ships. NOTE: expect multiple detections; the scorer's first-match-wins will tie this to the first actual detection matching Ferguson.
Honorific form appears dozens of times in prose on pages 2-3.
Complainant DOB in labelled table row. Phase 3 Example 12 labelled-DOB pattern test.
Complainant employee number — internal identifier that can re-identify an individual. Phase 3 Example 13 labelled-employee-number pattern test + Phase 5 label-adjacent regex target.
Complainant NZ driver licence in labelled table row. Phase 1 driver-licence regex test. Phase 3 Example 14 labelled-driver-licence pattern.

Complainant home address — suburb + postcode portion. The street address portion of the full row should also be caught by a broader address match; this substring entry guards against the multi-line cell truncation seen in prior redactions where only the street line was caught.
Complainant salary band — individual compensation info under s7(2)(a). Type choice deliberate: 'confidential' catch-all fits better than any dedicated type for salary PII.
